items.name: narrator
items.text: And when the Day of the Festival of weeks had come, they were all with one mind in one place.
items.kk: And when the Day of the Festival of weeks had come, they were all with one mind in one place.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And suddenly there came a sound from the shamayim, as of a rushing mighty ruach and it filled all the house where they were sitting.
items.kk: And suddenly there came a sound from the shah-mah-yeem, as of a rushing mighty roo-ahk and it filled all the house where they were sitting.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And there appeared to them divided tongues, as of fire and settled on each one of them.
items.kk: And there appeared to them divided tongues, as of fire and settled on each one of them.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And they were all filled with the Ruach HaQadash and began to speak with other tongues, as the Ruach gave them to speak.
items.kk: And they were all filled with the roo-ahk hah-kah-dahsh and began to speak with other tongues, as the roo-ahk gave them to speak.

items.name: narrator
items.text: Now in Yahrushalayim there were dwelling Yahuḏim, dedicated men from every nation under the shamayim.
items.kk: Now in yah-roo-shah-lah-yeem there were dwelling yah-hoo-deem, dedicated men from every nation under the shah-mah-yeem.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And when this sound came to be, the crowd came together and were confused, because everyone heard them speak in his own language.
items.kk: And when this sound came to be, the crowd came together and were confused, because everyone heard them speak in his own language.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And they were all amazed and marvelled, saying to each other,
items.kk: And they were all amazed and marvelled, saying to each other,

items.name: crowd at the festival of weeks
items.text: “Look, are not all these who speak Galileans?
items.kk: Look, are not all these who speak Galileans?

items.name: crowd at the festival of weeks
items.text: “And how do we hear, each one in our own language in which we were born?
items.kk: And how do we hear, each one in our own language in which we were born?

items.name: crowd at the festival of weeks
items.text: “Parthians and Medes and Ĕylamites and those dwelling in Aram Naharayim, both Yahuḏah and Kappadokia, Pontos and Asia, both Phrygia and Pamphulia, Mitsrayim and the parts of Libya around Cyrene, visitors from Rome, both Yahuḏim and converts, “Cretans and Araḇs, we hear them speaking in our own tongues the great deeds of Aluahim.”
items.kk: Parthians and Medes and Eylamites and those dwelling in Aram Naharayim, both yah-hoo-dah and Kappadokia, Pontos and Asia, both Phrygia and Pamphulia, meets-rah-yeem and the parts of Libya around Cyrene, visitors from Rome, both yah-hoo-deem and converts, Cretans and Arabs, we hear them speaking in our own tongues the great deeds of al-oo-ah-heem.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And they were all amazed and were puzzled, saying to each other,
items.kk: And they were all amazed and were puzzled, saying to each other,

items.name: crowd at the festival of weeks
items.text: “What does this mean?”
items.kk: What does this mean?

items.name: narrator
items.text: And others mocking said,
items.kk: And others mocking said,

items.text: “They have been filled with sweet wine.”
items.kk: They have been filled with sweet wine.

items.name: narrator
items.text: But Kĕpha, standing up with the eleven, lifted up his voice and said to them,
items.kk: But kay-fah, standing up with the eleven, lifted up his voice and said to them,

items.name: shimon
items.text: “Men of Yahuḏah and all those dwelling in Yahrushalayim, let this be known to you and listen closely to my words.
items.kk: Men of yah-hoo-dah and all those dwelling in yah-roo-shah-lah-yeem, let this be known to you and listen closely to my words.

items.name: shimon
items.text: “For these men are not drunk, as you imagine, since it is only the third hour of the day.
items.kk: For these men are not drunk, as you imagine, since it is only the third hour of the day.

items.name: shimon
items.text: “But this is what was spoken by the naḇi Yo’al:
items.kk: But this is what was spoken by the nah-vee Yoal,

items.name: shimon
items.text: ‘And it shall be in the last days, says Aluahim, that I shall pour out of My Ruach on all flesh. And your sons and your daughters shall prophesy and your young men shall see visions and your old men shall dream dreams,
items.kk: And it shall be in the last days, says al-oo-ah-heem, that I shall pour out of My roo-ahk on all flesh. And your sons and your daughters shall prophesy and your young men shall see visions and your old men shall dream dreams,

items.name: shimon
items.text: ‘And it shall be that everyone who calls on the Name of (YAHUAH) HWHY shall be saved.’
items.kk: And it shall be that everyone who calls on the Name of YAHUAH shall be saved.

items.name: shimon
items.text: “Men of Yasharal, hear these words: Yahusha of Natsareth, a Man from Aluahim, having been pointed out to you by mighty works and wonders and signs which Aluahim did through Him in your midst, as you yourselves also know,
items.kk: Men of yah-shar-al, hear these words, yah-hoo-shah of nahts-ah-ret, a Man from al-oo-ah-heem, having been pointed out to you by mighty works and wonders and signs which al-oo-ah-heem did through Him in your midst, as you yourselves also know,

items.name: shimon
items.text: this One, given up by the set purpose and foreknowledge of Aluahim, you have impaled and put to death through the hands of lawless men –
items.kk: this One, given up by the set purpose and foreknowledge of al-oo-ah-heem, you have impaled and put to death through the hands of lawless men,

items.name: shimon
items.text: “Him Aluahim raised up, having loosed the pangs of death because it was impossible that He could be held in its grip.
items.kk: Him al-oo-ah-heem raised up, having loosed the pangs of death because it was impossible that He could be held in its grip.

items.name: shimon
items.text: “Aluahim has raised up this Yahusha, of which we are all witnesses.
items.kk: al-oo-ah-heem has raised up this yah-hoo-shah, of which we are all witnesses.

items.name: shimon
items.text: “Therefore, having been exalted to the right hand of Aluahim and having received from the Father the promise of the Ruach HaQadash, He poured out this which you now see and hear.
items.kk: Therefore, having been exalted to the right hand of al-oo-ah-heem and having received from the Father the promise of the roo-ahk hah-kah-dahsh, He poured out this which you now see and hear.

items.name: shimon
items.text: “Therefore let all the house of Yasharal know for certain that Aluahim has made this Yahusha, whom you impaled, both Master and Mashiach.”
items.kk: Therefore let all the house of yah-shar-al know for certain that al-oo-ah-heem has made this yah-hoo-shah, whom you impaled, both Master and mah-shee-ahk.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And having heard this, they were pierced to the heart and said to Kĕpha and the rest of the emissaries,
items.kk: And having heard this, they were pierced to the heart and said to kay-fah and the rest of the emissaries,

items.name: crowd at the festival of weeks
items.text: “Men, brothers, what shall we do?”
items.kk: Men, brothers, what shall we do?

items.name: narrator
items.text: And Kĕpha said to them,
items.kk: And kay-fah said to them,

items.name: shimon
items.text: “Repent and let each one of you be immersed in the Name of Yahusha Mashiach for the forgiveness of sins and you shall receive the gift of the Ruach HaQadash.
items.kk: Repent and let each one of you be immersed in the Name of yah-hoo-shah mah-shee-ahk for the forgiveness of sins and you shall receive the gift of the roo-ahk hah-kah-dahsh.

items.name: shimon
items.text: “For the promise is to you and to your children and to all who are far off, as many as (YAHUAH) HWHY our Aluahim shall call.”
items.kk: For the promise is to you and to your children and to all who are far off, as many as YAHUAH our al-oo-ah-heem shall call.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And with many other words he earnestly witnessed and urged them, saying,
items.kk: And with many other words he earnestly witnessed and urged them, saying,

items.name: shimon
items.text: “Be saved from this crooked generation.”
items.kk: Be saved from this crooked generation.

items.name: narrator
items.text: Then those, indeed, who gladly received his word, were immersed. And on that day about three thousand beings were added to them.
items.kk: Then those, indeed, who gladly received his word, were immersed. And on that day about three thousand beings were added to them.

items.name: narrator
items.text: You hear it — the speech of your own village, from the mouth of a fisherman of Galil who has never been there.
items.kk: You hear it, the speech of your own village, from the mouth of a fisherman of gah-leel who has never been there.

items.name: narrator
items.text: Three thousand. The pools below the House are full all day, and the steps are wet to the top.
items.kk: Three thousand. The pools below the House are full all day, and the steps are wet to the top.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And they were continuing steadfastly in the teaching of the emissaries and in the fellowship and in the breaking of bread and in the prayers.
items.kk: And they were continuing steadfastly in the teaching of the emissaries and in the fellowship and in the breaking of bread and in the prayers.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And fear came upon every being and many wonders and signs were being done through the emissaries.
items.kk: And fear came upon every being and many wonders and signs were being done through the emissaries.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And all those who believed were together and had all in common,
items.kk: And all those who believed were together and had all in common,

items.name: narrator
items.text: and sold their possessions and property and divided them among all, as anyone might have need.
items.kk: and sold their possessions and property and divided them among all, as anyone might have need.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And day by day, continuing with one mind in the Qodash (Set Apart Place) and breaking bread from house to house, they ate their food with gladness and simplicity of heart,
items.kk: And day by day, continuing with one mind in the koh-dahsh and breaking bread from house to house, they ate their food with gladness and simplicity of heart,

items.name: narrator
items.text: praising Aluahim and having chen with all the people. And the Master added to the qahal those who were being saved, day by day.
items.kk: praising al-oo-ah-heem and having khen with all the people. And the Master added to the qahal those who were being saved, day by day.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And the group of those who believed were of one heart and one being. And no one claimed that any of his possessions was his own, but they had all in common.
items.kk: And the group of those who believed were of one heart and one being. And no one claimed that any of his possessions was his own, but they had all in common.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And with great power the emissaries gave witness to the resurrection of the Master Yahusha and great chen was upon them all.
items.kk: And with great power the emissaries gave witness to the resurrection of the Master yah-hoo-shah and great khen was upon them all.

items.name: narrator
items.text: For there was not anyone needy among them, for all who were possessors of lands or houses sold them and brought the prices of what was sold,
items.kk: For there was not anyone needy among them, for all who were possessors of lands or houses sold them and brought the prices of what was sold,

items.name: narrator
items.text: and laid them at the feet of the emissaries and they distributed to each as anyone had need.
items.kk: and laid them at the feet of the emissaries and they distributed to each as anyone had need.

items.name: narrator
items.text: You have not much. You lay it down with the rest. A widow from Hebron takes bread from the same basket.
items.kk: You have not much. You lay it down with the rest. A widow from Hebron takes bread from the same basket.

items.name: narrator
items.text: Gladness and simplicity of heart. You had not known there was such a thing to eat with.
items.kk: Gladness and simplicity of heart. You had not known there was such a thing to eat with.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And Kĕpha and Yahuchanon were going up to the Qodash (Set Apart Place) at the hour of prayer, the ninth hour.
items.kk: And kay-fah and yah-hoo-kah-nohn were going up to the koh-dahsh at the hour of prayer, the ninth hour.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And a certain man, lame from his birth, was carried, whom they laid daily at the gate of the Qodash (Set Apart Place) which is called Yaphah, to ask alms from those entering into the Qodash (Set Apart Place),
items.kk: And a certain man, lame from his birth, was carried, whom they laid daily at the gate of the koh-dahsh which is called Yaphah, to ask alms from those entering into the koh-dahsh,

items.name: narrator
items.text: who, seeing Kĕpha and Yahuchanon about to go into the Qodash (Set Apart Place), asked for alms.
items.kk: who, seeing kay-fah and yah-hoo-kah-nohn about to go into the koh-dahsh, asked for alms.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And Kĕpha, with Yahuchanon, looking steadfastly at him, said,
items.kk: And kay-fah, with yah-hoo-kah-nohn, looking steadfastly at him, said,

items.name: shimon
items.text: “Look at us.”
items.kk: Look at us.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And he gave heed to them, expecting to receive whatever from them.
items.kk: And he gave heed to them, expecting to receive whatever from them.

items.name: shimon
items.text: “I do not have silver and gold, but what I do possess, this I give you: In the Name of Yahusha Mashiach of Natsareth, rise up and walk.”
items.kk: I do not have silver and gold, but what I do possess, this I give you, In the Name of yah-hoo-shah mah-shee-ahk of nahts-ah-ret, rise up and walk.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And taking him by the right hand he lifted him up and immediately his feet and ankle bones were made firm.
items.kk: And taking him by the right hand he lifted him up and immediately his feet and ankle bones were made firm.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And leaping up, he stood and walked and went in with them into the Qodash (Set Apart Place), walking and leaping and praising Aluahim.
items.kk: And leaping up, he stood and walked and went in with them into the koh-dahsh, walking and leaping and praising al-oo-ah-heem.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And all the people saw him walking and praising Aluahim.
items.kk: And all the people saw him walking and praising al-oo-ah-heem.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And they recognised him, that it was he who sat begging alms at the Lovely Gate of the Qodash (Set Apart Place). And they were filled with wonder and amazement at what befell him.
items.kk: And they recognised him, that it was he who sat begging alms at the Lovely Gate of the koh-dahsh. And they were filled with wonder and amazement at what befell him.

items.name: narrator
items.text: You have walked past him every Pesach since you were a boy. You never once looked at his feet.
items.kk: You have walked past him every peh-sahk since you were a boy. You never once looked at his feet.

items.name: narrator
items.text: He is still leaping. Nobody tells him to stop.
items.kk: He is still leaping. Nobody tells him to stop.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And Stephanos, filled with belief and power, did great wonders and signs among the people.
items.kk: And Stephanos, filled with belief and power, did great wonders and signs among the people.

items.name: narrator
items.text: But some of those of the so called Qahal of the Freedmen (Cyrenians, Alexandrians and those from Kilikia and Asia), rose up, disputing with Stephanos,
items.kk: But some of those of the so called Qahal of the Freedmen Cyrenians, Alexandrians and those from Kilikia and Asia, rose up, disputing with Stephanos,

items.name: narrator
items.text: but they were unable to resist the wisdom and the Ruach by which he spoke.
items.kk: but they were unable to resist the wisdom and the roo-ahk by which he spoke.

items.name: narrator
items.text: Then they instigated men to say,
items.kk: Then they instigated men to say,

items.name: men
items.text: “We have heard him speak blasphemous words against Mosheh and Aluahim.”
items.kk: We have heard him speak blasphemous words against Mosheh and al-oo-ah-heem.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And they stirred up the people and the elders and the scribes, so they came upon him, seized him and brought him to the council.
items.kk: And they stirred up the people and the elders and the scribes, so they came upon him, seized him and brought him to the council.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And they set up false witnesses who said,
items.kk: And they set up false witnesses who said,

items.name: false
items.text: “This man does not cease to speak blasphemous words against this Qodash (Set Apart Place) and the Torah,
items.kk: This man does not cease to speak blasphemous words against this koh-dahsh and the toh-rah,

items.name: false
items.text: for we have heard him saying that this Yahusha of Natsareth shall overthrow this place and change the institutes which Mosheh delivered unto us.”
items.kk: for we have heard him saying that this yah-hoo-shah of nahts-ah-ret shall overthrow this place and change the institutes which Mosheh delivered unto us.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And all who sat in the council, looking steadily at him, saw his face was like the face of a heavenly mal'ak.
items.kk: And all who sat in the council, looking steadily at him, saw his face was like the face of a heavenly mahl-ahk.

items.name: narrator
items.text: The kohen gadol said,
items.kk: The kohen gadol said,

items.name: qayapha
items.text: “Is this so?”
items.kk: Is this so?

items.name: narrator
items.text: And he replied,
items.kk: And he replied,

items.name: stephanos
items.text: “Men, brothers and fathers, listen: The Aluahim of esteem appeared to our father Aḇrahim when he was in Aram Naharayim, before he dwelt in Ḥaran,
items.kk: Men, brothers and fathers, listen, The al-oo-ah-heem of esteem appeared to our father Abrahim when he was in Aram Naharayim, before he dwelt in Karan,

items.name: narrator
items.text: Stephanos tells them the whole history of their fathers — Aḇrahim, Yosĕph, Mosheh in the wilderness, the tent of witness, the house Shelomoh built. This is how he ends.
items.kk: Stephanos tells them the whole history of their fathers, Abrahim, yoh-sef, Mosheh in the wilderness, the tent of witness, the house Shelomoh built. This is how he ends.

items.name: stephanos
items.text: “However, the Most High does not dwell in dwellings made with hands, as the naḇi says:
items.kk: However, the Most High does not dwell in dwellings made with hands, as the nah-vee says,

items.name: stephanos
items.text: ‘The shamayim is My throne and earth is My footstool. What house shall you build for Me? says (YAHUAH) HWHY, or what is the place of My rest? ‘Has My hand not made all these?’
items.kk: The shah-mah-yeem is My throne and earth is My footstool. What house shall you build for Me? says YAHUAH, or what is the place of My rest? Has My hand not made all these?

items.name: stephanos
items.text: “You stiff-necked and uncircumcised in heart and ears! You always resist the Ruach HaQadash, as your fathers did, you also do.
items.kk: You stiff-necked and uncircumcised in heart and ears! You always resist the roo-ahk hah-kah-dahsh, as your fathers did, you also do.

items.name: stephanos
items.text: “Which of the naḇi'im did your fathers not persecute? They killed those who before announced the coming of the righteous One, of whom you now have become the betrayers and murderers,
items.kk: Which of the nabiim did your fathers not persecute? They killed those who before announced the coming of the righteous One, of whom you now have become the betrayers and murderers,

items.name: stephanos
items.text: who received the Torah as it was ordained by mal'akim, but did not watch over it.”
items.kk: who received the toh-rah as it was ordained by mahl-ah-keem, but did not watch over it.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And hearing this they were cut to the hearts and gnashed the teeth at him.
items.kk: And hearing this they were cut to the hearts and gnashed the teeth at him.

items.name: narrator
items.text: But he, being filled with the Ruach HaQadash, looked steadily into the shamayim and saw the esteem of Aluahim and Yahusha standing at the right hand of Aluahim,
items.kk: But he, being filled with the roo-ahk hah-kah-dahsh, looked steadily into the shah-mah-yeem and saw the esteem of al-oo-ah-heem and yah-hoo-shah standing at the right hand of al-oo-ah-heem,

items.text: and he said,
items.kk: and he said,

items.text: “Look! I see the shamayim opened and the Son of Aḏam standing at the right hand of Aluahim!”
items.kk: Look! I see the shah-mah-yeem opened and the Son of Adam standing at the right hand of al-oo-ah-heem!

items.name: narrator
items.text: And crying out with a loud voice, they stopped their ears and rushed upon him with one mind,
items.kk: And crying out with a loud voice, they stopped their ears and rushed upon him with one mind,

items.text: and threw him out of the city and stoned him. And the witnesses laid down their garments at the feet of a young man named Sha’ul.
items.kk: and threw him out of the city and stoned him. And the witnesses laid down their garments at the feet of a young man named Shaul.

items.name: narrator
items.text: What was done to Stephanos is told here as the Besorah tells it. It is not shown.
items.kk: What was done to Stephanos is told here as the beh-soh-rah tells it. It is not shown.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And they were stoning Stephanos as he was calling and saying,
items.kk: And they were stoning Stephanos as he was calling and saying,

items.name: stephanos
items.text: “Master Yahusha, receive my ruach.”
items.kk: Master yah-hoo-shah, receive my roo-ahk.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And kneeling down he cried out with a loud voice,
items.kk: And kneeling down he cried out with a loud voice,

items.text: “Master, do not hold this sin against them.”
items.kk: Master, do not hold this sin against them.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And having said this, he fell asleep.
items.kk: And having said this, he fell asleep.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And Sha’ul was giving approval to his death. And on that day there was a great persecution against the qahal which was at Yahrushalayim and they were all scattered throughout the countries of Yahuḏah and Shomeron, except the emissaries.

items.text: "Do not hold this sin against them." You have heard those words before, on a hill outside another gate.

items.text: “Go near and join him in that chariot.”
items.kk: Go near and join him in that chariot.

items.kk: Do you know what you are reading?

items.name: eunuch
items.text: “How am I able, unless someone guides me?”
items.kk: How am I able, unless someone guides me?

items.name: narrator
items.text: And he called Philip near, to come up and sit with him.
items.kk: And he called Philip near, to come up and sit with him.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And the passage of the Scripture which he was reading was this,
items.kk: And the passage of the Scripture which he was reading was this,

items.name: eunuch
items.text: “He was led as a sheep to slaughter and like a lamb silent before its shearer, so He opened not His mouth.
items.kk: He was led as a sheep to slaughter and like a lamb silent before its shearer, so He opened not His mouth.

items.name: eunuch
items.text: “In His humiliation He was deprived of right-ruling. And who shall declare His generation? Because His life was taken from the earth.”
items.kk: In His humiliation He was deprived of right-ruling. And who shall declare His generation? Because His life was taken from the earth.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And the eunuch, answering Philip, said,
items.kk: And the eunuch, answering Philip, said,

items.name: eunuch
items.text: “I ask you, about whom does the naḇi say this, about himself or about some other?”
items.kk: I ask you, about whom does the nah-vee say this, about himself or about some other?

items.name: narrator
items.text: And Philip opening his mouth and beginning at this Scripture, brought to him the Besorah: Yahusha!
items.kk: And Philip opening his mouth and beginning at this Scripture, brought to him the beh-soh-rah, yah-hoo-shah!

items.name: narrator
items.text: As they were going on the way, they came to some water. And the eunuch said,
items.kk: As they were going on the way, they came to some water. And the eunuch said,

items.name: eunuch
items.text: “Look, water! What hinders me from being immersed?”
items.kk: Look, water! What hinders me from being immersed?

items.name: narrator
items.text: And Philip said,
items.kk: And Philip said,

items.name: philip
items.text: “If you believe with all your heart, it is permitted.”
items.kk: If you believe with all your heart, it is permitted.

items.name: eunuch
items.text: “I believe that Yahusha Mashiach is the Son of Aluahim.”
items.kk: I believe that yah-hoo-shah mah-shee-ahk is the Son of al-oo-ah-heem.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And he commanded the chariot to stand still. And both Philip and the eunuch went down into the water and he immersed him.
items.kk: And he commanded the chariot to stand still. And both Philip and the eunuch went down into the water and he immersed him.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And when they came up out of the water, the Ruach of (YAHUAH) HWHY caught Philip away and the eunuch saw him no more, for he went his way, rejoicing.
items.kk: And when they came up out of the water, the roo-ahk of YAHUAH caught Philip away and the eunuch saw him no more, for he went his way, rejoicing.

items.name: narrator
items.text: Philip, however, was found at Ashdoḏ. And passing through, he brought the Besorah in all the cities until he came to Caesarea.
items.kk: Philip, however, was found at Ashdod. And passing through, he brought the beh-soh-rah in all the cities until he came to Caesarea.

items.name: narrator
items.text: South, toward Kush, at the edge of the world. He is singing. You can hear it a long way down the road.
items.kk: South, toward Kush, at the edge of the world. He is singing. You can hear it a long way down the road.

items.name: narrator
items.text: There is no one at the water but you, and the reeds, and his footprints going in.
items.kk: There is no one at the water but you, and the reeds, and his footprints going in.

items.name: narrator
items.text: But Sha’ul, still breathing threats and murder against the taught ones of the Master, having come to the kohen gadol,
items.kk: But Shaul, still breathing threats and murder against the taught ones of the Master, having come to the kohen gadol,

items.name: narrator
items.text: asked from him letters to the qahalim of Damascus, so that if he found any who were of the Way, whether men or women, to bring them bound to Yahrushalayim.
items.kk: asked from him letters to the qahalim of Damascus, so that if he found any who were of the Way, whether men or women, to bring them bound to yah-roo-shah-lah-yeem.

items.name: narrator
items.text: It came to be, that as he journeyed, he came near Damascus and suddenly a light flashed around him from the shamayim.
items.kk: It came to be, that as he journeyed, he came near Damascus and suddenly a light flashed around him from the shah-mah-yeem.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And he fell to the ground and heard a voice saying to him,
items.kk: And he fell to the ground and heard a voice saying to him,

items.name: yahusha mashiach
items.text: “Sha’ul, Sha’ul, why do you persecute Me?”
items.kk: Shaul, Shaul, why do you persecute Me?

items.name: shaul
items.text: “Who are You, Master?”
items.kk: Who are You, Master?

items.name: narrator
items.text: And the Master said,
items.kk: And the Master said,

items.name: yahusha mashiach
items.text: “I am Yahusha, whom you persecute. It is hard for you to kick against the prods.”
items.kk: I am yah-hoo-shah, whom you persecute. It is hard for you to kick against the prods.

items.name: narrator
items.text: Both trembling and being astonished, he said,
items.kk: Both trembling and being astonished, he said,

items.name: shaul
items.text: “Master, what do You wish me to do?”
items.kk: Master, what do You wish me to do?

items.name: narrator
items.text: And the Master said to him,
items.kk: And the Master said to him,

items.name: yahusha mashiach
items.text: “Arise and go into the city and you shall be told what you have to do.”
items.kk: Arise and go into the city and you shall be told what you have to do.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And the men journeying with him stood speechless, hearing indeed the voice but seeing no one.
items.kk: And the men journeying with him stood speechless, hearing indeed the voice but seeing no one.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And Sha’ul arose from the ground, but when his eyes were opened he saw no one. And leading him by the hand they brought him into Damascus.
items.kk: And Shaul arose from the ground, but when his eyes were opened he saw no one. And leading him by the hand they brought him into Damascus.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And he was three days without sight and did not eat nor drink.
items.kk: And he was three days without sight and did not eat nor drink.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And there was at Damascus a certain taught one, by name Ḥananyah. And the Master said unto him in a vision,
items.kk: And there was at Damascus a certain taught one, by name Kananyah. And the Master said unto him in a vision,

items.name: yahusha mashiach
items.text: “Ḥananyah!”
items.kk: Kananyah!

items.name: hananyah
items.text: “Here I am, Master.”
items.kk: Here I am, Master.

items.name: yahusha mashiach
items.text: “Arise and go to the street called Straight and seek in the house of Yahuḏah for one called Sha’ul of Tarsos, for look, he is praying,
items.kk: Arise and go to the street called Straight and seek in the house of yah-hoo-dah for one called Shaul of Tarsos, for look, he is praying,

items.name: yahusha mashiach
items.text: and has seen in a vision a man named Ḥananyah coming in and laying his hand on him, so as to see again.”
items.kk: and has seen in a vision a man named Kananyah coming in and laying his hand on him, so as to see again.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And Ḥananyah answered,
items.kk: And Kananyah answered,

items.name: hananyah
items.text: “Master, I have heard from many about this man, how many evils he did to Your qadashiyms (Set Apart Ones) in Yahrushalayim,
items.kk: Master, I have heard from many about this man, how many evils he did to Your qadashiyms in yah-roo-shah-lah-yeem,

items.name: hananyah
items.text: and here he has authority from the chief kohanim to bind all those calling on Your Name.”
items.kk: and here he has authority from the chief koh-hah-neem to bind all those calling on Your Name.

items.name: narrator
items.text: But the Master said to him,
items.kk: But the Master said to him,

items.name: yahusha mashiach
items.text: “Go, for he is a chosen vessel of Mine to bear My Name before nations, sovereigns and the children of Yasharal.
items.kk: Go, for he is a chosen vessel of Mine to bear My Name before nations, sovereigns and the children of yah-shar-al.

items.name: yahusha mashiach
items.text: “For I shall show him how much he has to suffer for My Name.”
items.kk: For I shall show him how much he has to suffer for My Name.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And Ḥananyah went away and went into the house. And laying his hands on him he said,
items.kk: And Kananyah went away and went into the house. And laying his hands on him he said,

items.name: hananyah
items.text: “Brother Sha’ul, the Master Yahusha, who appeared to you on the way as you came, has sent me, so that you might see again and be filled with the Ruach HaQadash.”
items.kk: Brother Shaul, the Master yah-hoo-shah, who appeared to you on the way as you came, has sent me, so that you might see again and be filled with the roo-ahk hah-kah-dahsh.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And immediately there fell from his eyes, as it were scales and he received his sight. And rising up, he was immersed.
items.kk: And immediately there fell from his eyes, as it were scales and he received his sight. And rising up, he was immersed.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And having received food, he was strengthened. And Sha’ul was with the taught ones at Damascus some days.
items.kk: And having received food, he was strengthened. And Shaul was with the taught ones at Damascus some days.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And immediately he proclaimed the Mashiach in the qahalim, that He is the Son of Aluahim.
items.kk: And immediately he proclaimed the mah-shee-ahk in the qahalim, that He is the Son of al-oo-ah-heem.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And all who heard were amazed and said,
items.kk: And all who heard were amazed and said,

items.name: those in the qahalim of damascus
items.text: “Is this not he who destroyed those calling on this Name in Yahrushalayim and has come here for this, to take them bound to the chief kohanim?”
items.kk: Is this not he who destroyed those calling on this Name in yah-roo-shah-lah-yeem and has come here for this, to take them bound to the chief koh-hah-neem?

items.name: narrator
items.text: But Sha’ul kept increasing in strength and was confounding the Yahuḏim who dwelt in Damascus, proving that this is the Mashiach.
items.kk: But Shaul kept increasing in strength and was confounding the yah-hoo-deem who dwelt in Damascus, proving that this is the mah-shee-ahk.

items.name: narrator
items.text: Clear. The man who could not see three days ago is reading the scroll of Yahshayahu aloud in the qahal.
items.kk: Clear. The man who could not see three days ago is reading the scroll of yah-shah-yah-hoo aloud in the qahal.

items.name: narrator
items.text: You knew him at once. He does not know you. You do not tell him.
items.kk: You knew him at once. He does not know you. You do not tell him.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And on the next day, as they were on their way and approaching the city, Kĕpha went up on the house-top to pray, about the sixth hour.
items.kk: And on the next day, as they were on their way and approaching the city, kay-fah went up on the house-top to pray, about the sixth hour.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And he became hungry and wished to eat. But while they were preparing, he fell into a trance,
items.kk: And he became hungry and wished to eat. But while they were preparing, he fell into a trance,

items.name: narrator
items.text: and he saw the shamayim opened and a certain vessel like a great sheet bound at the four corners, descending to him and let down to the earth,
items.kk: and he saw the shah-mah-yeem opened and a certain vessel like a great sheet bound at the four corners, descending to him and let down to the earth,

items.name: narrator
items.text: in which were all kinds of four-footed beasts of the earth, wild beasts, creeping creatures and the birds of the shamayim.
items.kk: in which were all kinds of four-footed beasts of the earth, wild beasts, creeping creatures and the birds of the shah-mah-yeem.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And a voice came to him,
items.kk: And a voice came to him,

items.name: divine
items.text: “Rise up, Kĕpha, slay and eat.”
items.kk: Rise up, kay-fah, slay and eat.

items.name: shimon
items.text: “Not at all, Master! Because I have never eaten whatever is common or unclean.”
items.kk: Not at all, Master! Because I have never eaten whatever is common or unclean.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And a voice came to him again the second time,
items.kk: And a voice came to him again the second time,

items.name: divine
items.text: “What Aluahim has cleansed you do not consider common.”
items.kk: What al-oo-ah-heem has cleansed you do not consider common.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And this took place three times and the vessel was taken back to the shamayim.
items.kk: And this took place three times and the vessel was taken back to the shah-mah-yeem.

items.name: narrator
items.text: While Kĕpha was doubting within himself about what the vision might mean, look, the men who had been sent from Cornelius, having asked for the house of Shim‛on, stood at the gate,
items.kk: While kay-fah was doubting within himself about what the vision might mean, look, the men who had been sent from Cornelius, having asked for the house of sheem-ohn, stood at the gate,

items.name: narrator
items.text: and calling out, they enquired whether Shim‛on, also known as Kĕpha, was staying there.
items.kk: and calling out, they enquired whether sheem-ohn, also known as kay-fah, was staying there.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And as Kĕpha was thinking about the vision, the Ruach said to him,
items.kk: And as kay-fah was thinking about the vision, the roo-ahk said to him,

items.name: divine
items.text: “See, three men seek you.
items.kk: See, three men seek you.

items.name: divine
items.text: “But rise up, go down and go with them, not doubting at all, for I have sent them.”
items.kk: But rise up, go down and go with them, not doubting at all, for I have sent them.

items.name: narrator
items.text: So Kĕpha went down to the men who had been sent to him from Cornelius and said,
items.kk: So kay-fah went down to the men who had been sent to him from Cornelius and said,

items.name: shimon
items.text: “Look, I am the one you seek. Why have you come?”
items.kk: Look, I am the one you seek. Why have you come?

items.name: men
items.text: “Cornelius the captain, a righteous man and one who fears Aluahim and well spoken of by the entire nation of the Yahuḏim, was instructed by a qadash (Set Apart) mal'ak to send for you to his house and to hear words from you.”
items.kk: Cornelius the captain, a righteous man and one who fears al-oo-ah-heem and well spoken of by the entire nation of the yah-hoo-deem, was instructed by a kah-dahsh mahl-ahk to send for you to his house and to hear words from you.

items.name: narrator
items.text: So inviting them in, he housed them. And on the next day Kĕpha went away with them and some brothers from Yapho went with him.
items.kk: So inviting them in, he housed them. And on the next day kay-fah went away with them and some brothers from Yapho went with him.

items.name: narrator
items.text: A Roman, at a Yahudi gate, asking for a fisherman by name. Kĕpha takes him in and gives him a bed.
items.kk: A Roman, at a Yahudi gate, asking for a fisherman by name. kay-fah takes him in and gives him a bed.

items.name: narrator
items.text: He looks at the sky for a while. "Nothing that Aluahim has cleansed," he says at last, "is common."
items.kk: He looks at the sky for a while. Nothing that al-oo-ah-heem has cleansed, he says at last, is common.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And the following day they entered into Caesarea. And Cornelius was waiting for them, having called together his relatives and close friends.
items.kk: And the following day they entered into Caesarea. And Cornelius was waiting for them, having called together his relatives and close friends.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And it came to be, that when Kĕpha entered, Cornelius met him and fell down at his feet and bowed before him.
items.kk: And it came to be, that when kay-fah entered, Cornelius met him and fell down at his feet and bowed before him.

items.name: narrator
items.text: But Kĕpha raised him up, saying,
items.kk: But kay-fah raised him up, saying,

items.name: shimon
items.text: “Stand up, I myself am also a man.”
items.kk: Stand up, I myself am also a man.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And talking with him, he went in and found many who had come together.
items.kk: And talking with him, he went in and found many who had come together.

items.name: shimon
items.text: “You know that a Yahudi man is not allowed to associate with, or go to one of another race. But Aluahim has shown me that I should not call any man common or unclean.
items.kk: You know that a Yahudi man is not allowed to associate with, or go to one of another race. But al-oo-ah-heem has shown me that I should not call any man common or unclean.

items.name: shimon
items.text: “That is why I came without hesitation when I was sent for. So I ask, why have you sent for me?”
items.kk: That is why I came without hesitation when I was sent for. So I ask, why have you sent for me?

items.name: narrator
items.text: And Cornelius said,
items.kk: And Cornelius said,

items.name: cornelius
items.text: “Four days ago I was fasting until this hour. And at the ninth hour I prayed in my house and see, a man stood before me in shining garments,
items.kk: Four days ago I was fasting until this hour. And at the ninth hour I prayed in my house and see, a man stood before me in shining garments,

items.name: cornelius
items.text: and said, ‘Cornelius, your prayer has been heard and your kind deeds were remembered before Aluahim.
items.kk: and said, Cornelius, your prayer has been heard and your kind deeds were remembered before al-oo-ah-heem.

items.name: cornelius
items.text: ‘Now send to Yapho and call Shim‛on here, who is also called Kĕpha. He is staying in the house of Shim‛on, a leather tanner, by the sea. When he comes, he shall speak to you.’
items.kk: Now send to Yapho and call sheem-ohn here, who is also called kay-fah. He is staying in the house of sheem-ohn, a leather tanner, by the sea. When he comes, he shall speak to you.

items.name: cornelius
items.text: “So I sent to you immediately and you have done well to come. And now, we are all present before Aluahim, to hear all that you have been commanded by Aluahim.”
items.kk: So I sent to you immediately and you have done well to come. And now, we are all present before al-oo-ah-heem, to hear all that you have been commanded by al-oo-ah-heem.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And opening his mouth, Kĕpha said,
items.kk: And opening his mouth, kay-fah said,

items.name: shimon
items.text: “Truly I see that Aluahim shows no partiality,
items.kk: Truly I see that al-oo-ah-heem shows no partiality,

items.name: shimon
items.text: but in every nation, he who fears Him and works righteousness is accepted by Him.
items.kk: but in every nation, he who fears Him and works righteousness is accepted by Him.

items.name: shimon
items.text: ”He sent the word to the children of Yasharal, bringing the Besorah: shalom through Yahusha Mashiach! He is Master of all.
items.kk: He sent the word to the children of yah-shar-al, bringing the beh-soh-rah, shah-lohm through yah-hoo-shah mah-shee-ahk! He is Master of all.

items.name: shimon
items.text: how Aluahim did anoint Yahusha of Natsareth with the Ruach HaQadash and with power, who went about doing good and healing all who were oppressed by the devil, for Aluahim was with Him.
items.kk: how al-oo-ah-heem did anoint yah-hoo-shah of nahts-ah-ret with the roo-ahk hah-kah-dahsh and with power, who went about doing good and healing all who were oppressed by the devil, for al-oo-ah-heem was with Him.

items.name: shimon
items.text: “And we are witnesses of all He did, both in the country of the Yahuḏim and in Yahrushalayim, whom they even killed by hanging on a timber.
items.kk: And we are witnesses of all He did, both in the country of the yah-hoo-deem and in yah-roo-shah-lah-yeem, whom they even killed by hanging on a timber.

items.name: shimon
items.text: “Aluahim raised up this One on the third day and let Him be seen,
items.kk: al-oo-ah-heem raised up this One on the third day and let Him be seen,

items.name: shimon
items.text: not to all the people, but to witnesses, those having been chosen before by Aluahim – to us who ate and drank with Him after He arose from the dead.
items.kk: not to all the people, but to witnesses, those having been chosen before by al-oo-ah-heem, to us who ate and drank with Him after He arose from the dead.

items.name: shimon
items.text: “And He commanded us to proclaim to the people and to witness that it is He who was appointed by Aluahim to be Judge of the living and the dead.
items.kk: And He commanded us to proclaim to the people and to witness that it is He who was appointed by al-oo-ah-heem to be Judge of the living and the dead.

items.name: shimon
items.text: “To this One all the naḇi'im bear witness, that through His Name, everyone believing in Him does receive forgiveness of sins.”
items.kk: To this One all the nabiim bear witness, that through His Name, everyone believing in Him does receive forgiveness of sins.

items.name: narrator
items.text: While Kĕpha was still speaking these words, the Ruach HaQadash fell upon all those hearing the word.
items.kk: While kay-fah was still speaking these words, the roo-ahk hah-kah-dahsh fell upon all those hearing the word.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And those of the circumcision who believed were astonished, as many as came with Kĕpha, because the gift of the Ruach HaQadash had been poured out on the gentiles also,
items.kk: And those of the circumcision who believed were astonished, as many as came with kay-fah, because the gift of the roo-ahk hah-kah-dahsh had been poured out on the gentiles also,

items.name: narrator
items.text: for they were hearing them speaking with tongues and extolling Aluahim. Then Kĕpha answered,
items.kk: for they were hearing them speaking with tongues and extolling al-oo-ah-heem. Then kay-fah answered,

items.name: shimon
items.text: “Is anyone able to forbid water, that these should not be immersed who have received the Ruach HaQadash – even as also we?”
items.kk: Is anyone able to forbid water, that these should not be immersed who have received the roo-ahk hah-kah-dahsh, even as also we?

items.name: narrator
items.text: And he commanded them to be immersed in the Name of Yahusha Mashiach. Then they asked him to remain a few days.
items.kk: And he commanded them to be immersed in the Name of yah-hoo-shah mah-shee-ahk. Then they asked him to remain a few days.

items.name: narrator
items.text: A captain of the Italian regiment, his soldiers, his slaves, his wife's brothers. The fire came on them as it came on the eleven in the upper room. Kĕpha cannot stop smiling.
items.kk: A captain of the Italian regiment, his soldiers, his slaves, his wife's brothers. The fire came on them as it came on the eleven in the upper room. kay-fah cannot stop smiling.

items.name: narrator
items.text: "Make taught ones of all the nations." Here is the first house of them.
items.kk: Make taught ones of all the nations. Here is the first house of them.

items.name: narrator
items.text: Then, indeed, they who were scattered because of the pressure that arose over Stephanos passed through to Phoenicia and Cyprus and Antioch, speaking the word to no one except the Yahuḏim only.
items.kk: Then, indeed, they who were scattered because of the pressure that arose over Stephanos passed through to Phoenicia and Cyprus and Antioch, speaking the word to no one except the yah-hoo-deem only.

items.name: narrator
items.text: But some of them were men from Cyprus and Cyrene, who, when they had come to Antioch, spoke to the Hellenists, bringing the Besorah: the Master Yahusha!
items.kk: But some of them were men from Cyprus and Cyrene, who, when they had come to Antioch, spoke to the Hellenists, bringing the beh-soh-rah, the Master yah-hoo-shah!

items.name: narrator
items.text: And the hand of the Master was with them and a great number having believed turned to the Master.
items.kk: And the hand of the Master was with them and a great number having believed turned to the Master.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And word of it came to the ears of the qahal in Yahrushalayim and they sent out Barnaḇah to go as far as Antioch,
items.kk: And word of it came to the ears of the qahal in yah-roo-shah-lah-yeem and they sent out Barnabah to go as far as Antioch,

items.name: narrator
items.text: who, having come and seeing the chen of Aluahim, was glad and encouraged them all with purpose of heart to cleave to the Master.
items.kk: who, having come and seeing the khen of al-oo-ah-heem, was glad and encouraged them all with purpose of heart to cleave to the Master.

items.name: narrator
items.text: Because he was a good man and filled with the Ruach HaQadash and with belief. And large numbers were added to the Master.
items.kk: Because he was a good man and filled with the roo-ahk hah-kah-dahsh and with belief. And large numbers were added to the Master.

items.name: narrator
items.text: Then Barnaḇah went to Tarsos to seek Sha’ul,
items.kk: Then Barnabah went to Tarsos to seek Shaul,

items.name: narrator
items.text: and having found him, he brought him to Antioch. And it came to be that for an entire year they came together in the qahal and taught large numbers. And the taught ones were called ‘Natsarim’ first in Antioch.
items.kk: and having found him, he brought him to Antioch. And it came to be that for an entire year they came together in the qahal and taught large numbers. And the taught ones were called Natsarim first in Antioch.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And in the qahal that was at Antioch there were certain naḇi'im and teachers: both Barnaḇah and Shim‛on who was called Niger and Lucius of Cyrene and Manaḥĕm who had been brought up with Herodes the district ruler and Sha’ul.
items.kk: And in the qahal that was at Antioch there were certain nabiim and teachers, both Barnabah and sheem-ohn who was called Niger and Lucius of Cyrene and Manakem who had been brought up with Herodes the district ruler and Shaul.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And as they were doing service to the Master and fasted, the Ruach HaQadash said,
items.kk: And as they were doing service to the Master and fasted, the roo-ahk hah-kah-dahsh said,

items.name: divine
items.text: “Separate unto Me Barnaḇah and Sha’ul for the work to which I have called them.”
items.kk: Separate unto Me Barnabah and Shaul for the work to which I have called them.

items.name: narrator
items.text: Then having fasted and prayed and having laid hands on them, they sent them away.
items.kk: Then having fasted and prayed and having laid hands on them, they sent them away.

items.name: narrator
items.text: Natsarim. The people of Natsareth's man. They meant it as a joke here. It has stuck.
items.kk: Natsarim. The people of nahts-ah-rets man. They meant it as a joke here. It has stuck.

items.name: narrator
items.text: "Where the Ruach sends," Barnaḇah says. Sha’ul is already looking at the sea.
items.kk: Where the roo-ahk sends, Barnabah says. Shaul is already looking at the sea.

items.name: narrator
items.text: But while Sha’ul was waiting for them at Athens, his ruach was stirred up within him when he saw that the city was utterly idolatrous.
items.kk: But while Shaul was waiting for them at Athens, his roo-ahk was stirred up within him when he saw that the city was utterly idolatrous.

items.name: narrator
items.text: Therefore, indeed, he was reasoning in the qahal with the Yahuḏim and with the gentile worshippers and in the market-place daily with those who met there.
items.kk: Therefore, indeed, he was reasoning in the qahal with the yah-hoo-deem and with the gentile worshippers and in the market-place daily with those who met there.

items.name: narrator
items.text: Cut in the stone: ΑΓΝΩΣΤΩ ΘΕΩ — "to an unknown god". Such altars stood in Athens; the traveller Pausanias saw them on the road from the harbour.
items.kk: Cut in the stone, ΑΓΝΩΣΤΩ ΘΕΩ, to an unknown god. Such altars stood in Athens, the traveller Pausanias saw them on the road from the harbour.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And some of the Epicurean and Stoic philosophers encountered him. And some were saying,
items.kk: And some of the Epicurean and Stoic philosophers encountered him. And some were saying,

items.name: some
items.text: “What does this babbler wish to say?”
items.kk: What does this babbler wish to say?

items.name: narrator
items.text: Others said,
items.kk: Others said,

items.name: ph1
items.text: “He seems to be a proclaimer of strange mighty ones”
items.kk: He seems to be a proclaimer of strange mighty ones

items.name: narrator
items.text: – because to them he brought the Besorah: Yahusha and the resurrection!
items.kk: because to them he brought the beh-soh-rah, yah-hoo-shah and the resurrection!

items.name: narrator
items.text: So they laid hold of him and brought him to the Areopagus, saying,
items.kk: So they laid hold of him and brought him to the Areopagus, saying,

items.name: athenians
items.text: “Are we able to know what this fresh teaching is of which you speak?
items.kk: Are we able to know what this fresh teaching is of which you speak?

items.name: athenians
items.text: “For you are bringing some strange matters to our ears. We wish, then, to know what these mean.”
items.kk: For you are bringing some strange matters to our ears. We wish, then, to know what these mean.

items.name: narrator
items.text: For all the Athenians and the strangers living there spent their leisure time in doing naught but to speak or to hear what is fresh.
items.kk: For all the Athenians and the strangers living there spent their leisure time in doing naught but to speak or to hear what is fresh.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And having stood in the midst of the Areopagus Sha’ul said,
items.kk: And having stood in the midst of the Areopagus Shaul said,

items.name: shaul
items.text: “Men of Athens, I see that you are very religious in every matter.
items.kk: Men of Athens, I see that you are very religious in every matter.

items.name: shaul
items.text: “For passing through and observing the objects of your worship, I even found an mizbe'ach with this inscription:TO THE UNKNOWN MIGHTY ONE. Not knowing then whom you worship, I make Him known to you:
items.kk: For passing through and observing the objects of your worship, I even found an miz-beh-ahk with this inscription,to the unknown mighty one. Not knowing then whom you worship, I make Him known to you,

items.name: shaul
items.text: “(YAHUAH) HWHY, who made the world and all that is in it, this One being Master of shamayim and earth, does not dwell in dwellings made with hands.
items.kk: YAHUAH, who made the world and all that is in it, this One being Master of shah-mah-yeem and earth, does not dwell in dwellings made with hands.

items.name: shaul
items.text: “Nor is He served with men’s hands – as if needing any – Himself giving to all life and breath and all else.
items.kk: Nor is He served with men's hands, as if needing any, Himself giving to all life and breath and all else.

items.name: shaul
items.text: “And He has made from one blood every nation of men to dwell on all the face of the earth, having ordained beforehand the times and the boundaries of their dwelling,
items.kk: And He has made from one blood every nation of men to dwell on all the face of the earth, having ordained beforehand the times and the boundaries of their dwelling,

items.name: shaul
items.text: to seek the Master, if at least they would reach out for Him and find Him, though He is not far from each one of us.
items.kk: to seek the Master, if at least they would reach out for Him and find Him, though He is not far from each one of us.

items.name: shaul
items.text: “For in Him we live and move and are, as also some of your own poets have said, ‘For we are also His offspring.’
items.kk: For in Him we live and move and are, as also some of your own poets have said, For we are also His offspring.

items.name: shaul
items.text: “Now then, since we are the offspring of Aluahim, we should not think that the Aluahim is like gold or silver or stone, an image made by the skill and thought of man.
items.kk: Now then, since we are the offspring of al-oo-ah-heem, we should not think that the al-oo-ah-heem is like gold or silver or stone, an image made by the skill and thought of man.

items.name: shaul
items.text: “Truly, then, having overlooked these times of ignorance, Aluahim now commands all men everywhere to repent,
items.kk: Truly, then, having overlooked these times of ignorance, al-oo-ah-heem now commands all men everywhere to repent,

items.name: shaul
items.text: because He has set a day on which He is going to judge the world in righteousness by a Man whom He has appointed, having given proof of this to all by raising Him from the dead.”
items.kk: because He has set a day on which He is going to judge the world in righteousness by a Man whom He has appointed, having given proof of this to all by raising Him from the dead.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And hearing of the resurrection of the dead, some indeed mocked, while others said,
items.kk: And hearing of the resurrection of the dead, some indeed mocked, while others said,

items.name: athenians
items.text: “We shall hear you again concerning this.”
items.kk: We shall hear you again concerning this.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And so Sha’ul went out from among them.
items.kk: And so Shaul went out from among them.

items.name: narrator
items.text: But some men joined him and believed, among them Dionusios the Areopagite and a woman named Damaris and others with them.
items.kk: But some men joined him and believed, among them Dionusios the Areopagite and a woman named Damaris and others with them.

items.name: narrator
items.text: White marble, gold, the finest house ever built for a god, the Athenians say. "He does not dwell in dwellings made with hands."
items.kk: White marble, gold, the finest house ever built for a god, the Athenians say. He does not dwell in dwellings made with hands.

items.name: narrator
items.text: A judge of the hill of Ares, a woman named Damaris, a few others. That is all. It is enough to begin with.
items.kk: A judge of the hill of Ares, a woman named Damaris, a few others. That is all. It is enough to begin with.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And much time having passed and the sailing now being dangerous, because the Fast was already over, Sha’ul advised them,
items.kk: And much time having passed and the sailing now being dangerous, because the Fast was already over, Shaul advised them,

items.name: shaul
items.text: “Men, I see that this voyage is going to end with damage and great loss, not only of the cargo and ship, but also our lives.”
items.kk: Men, I see that this voyage is going to end with damage and great loss, not only of the cargo and ship, but also our lives.

items.name: narrator
items.text: But the captain was persuaded by the pilot and the owner of the ship, rather than what Sha’ul said.
items.kk: But the captain was persuaded by the pilot and the owner of the ship, rather than what Shaul said.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And a south ruach blowing softly, thinking they had obtained their purpose, having lifted anchor, they sailed along Crete, close inshore.
items.kk: And a south roo-ahk blowing softly, thinking they had obtained their purpose, having lifted anchor, they sailed along Crete, close inshore.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And not long after, a stormy head ruach rushed down from it, called Northeaster.
items.kk: And not long after, a stormy head roo-ahk rushed down from it, called Northeaster.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And when the ship was caught in it and unable to head against the ruach, we let her go and were driven.
items.kk: And when the ship was caught in it and unable to head against the roo-ahk, we let her go and were driven.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And because we were exceedingly storm-tossed, the next day they began to throw overboard.
items.kk: And because we were exceedingly storm-tossed, the next day they began to throw overboard.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And on the third day we threw out the ship’s tackle with our own hands.
items.kk: And on the third day we threw out the ship's tackle with our own hands.

items.name: narrator
items.text: When, now, neither sun nor stars appeared for many days and no small storm beat on us, all expectancy that we would be saved was taken away.
items.kk: When, now, neither sun nor stars appeared for many days and no small storm beat on us, all expectancy that we would be saved was taken away.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And when there had been a long abstinence from food, then Sha’ul, standing in the midst of them, said,
items.kk: And when there had been a long abstinence from food, then Shaul, standing in the midst of them, said,

items.name: shaul
items.text: “Truly, men, you should have listened to me not to have sailed from Crete and sustained this damage and loss.
items.kk: Truly, men, you should have listened to me not to have sailed from Crete and sustained this damage and loss.

items.name: shaul
items.text: “And now I urge you to take courage, for there shall be no loss of life among you, but only of the ship.
items.kk: And now I urge you to take courage, for there shall be no loss of life among you, but only of the ship.

items.name: shaul
items.text: “For tonight a mal'ak of the Aluahim to whom I belong and whom I serve, stood by me,
items.kk: For tonight a mahl-ahk of the al-oo-ah-heem to whom I belong and whom I serve, stood by me,

items.name: shaul
items.text: saying, ‘Do not be afraid, Sha’ul, you have to be brought before Caesar. And look, Aluahim has favourably given you all those who sail with you.’
items.kk: saying, Do not be afraid, Shaul, you have to be brought before Caesar. And look, al-oo-ah-heem has favourably given you all those who sail with you.

items.name: shaul
items.text: “Therefore take courage, men, for I believe Aluahim that it shall be according to the way it was spoken to me.
items.kk: Therefore take courage, men, for I believe al-oo-ah-heem that it shall be according to the way it was spoken to me.

items.name: shaul
items.text: “However, we need to run aground on some island.”
items.kk: However, we need to run aground on some island.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And when the fourteenth night came, as we were driven up and down in the Adriatic Sea, about midnight the sailors suspected that they were drawing near some land.
items.kk: And when the fourteenth night came, as we were driven up and down in the Adriatic Sea, about midnight the sailors suspected that they were drawing near some land.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And, fearing lest we should run aground on the rocks, they dropped four anchors from the stern and were praying for day to come.
items.kk: And, fearing lest we should run aground on the rocks, they dropped four anchors from the stern and were praying for day to come.

items.name: narrator
items.text: But when the sailors were seeking to escape from the ship, when they had let down the boat into the sea, under pretence of going to cast out anchors from the prow,
items.kk: But when the sailors were seeking to escape from the ship, when they had let down the boat into the sea, under pretence of going to cast out anchors from the prow,

items.name: narrator
items.text: Sha’ul said to the captain and the soldiers,
items.kk: Shaul said to the captain and the soldiers,

items.name: shaul
items.text: “If these do not remain in the ship, it is impossible for you to be saved.”
items.kk: If these do not remain in the ship, it is impossible for you to be saved.

items.name: narrator
items.text: Then the soldiers did cut the ropes of the boat and let it fall off.
items.kk: Then the soldiers did cut the ropes of the boat and let it fall off.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And when day was about to come, Sha’ul urged them all to take food, saying,
items.kk: And when day was about to come, Shaul urged them all to take food, saying,

items.name: shaul
items.text: “Today is the fourteenth day you have continued without food and eaten none at all.
items.kk: Today is the fourteenth day you have continued without food and eaten none at all.

items.name: shaul
items.text: “So I urge you to take food, for this concerns your safety, since not a hair shall fall from the head of any of you.”
items.kk: So I urge you to take food, for this concerns your safety, since not a hair shall fall from the head of any of you.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And having said this, he took bread and gave thanks to Aluahim in the presence of them all. And when he had broken it he began to eat.
items.kk: And having said this, he took bread and gave thanks to al-oo-ah-heem in the presence of them all. And when he had broken it he began to eat.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And they were all encouraged and also took food themselves.
items.kk: And they were all encouraged and also took food themselves.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And all of us were two hundred and seventy-six beings in the ship.
items.kk: And all of us were two hundred and seventy-six beings in the ship.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And when day came, they did not recognise the land, but they noted a certain bay with a beach, onto which they planned to run the ship if possible.
items.kk: And when day came, they did not recognise the land, but they noted a certain bay with a beach, onto which they planned to run the ship if possible.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And having cast off the anchors, they left them in the sea, meanwhile untying the rudder ropes. And they hoisted the foresail to the ruach and made for the beach.
items.kk: And having cast off the anchors, they left them in the sea, meanwhile untying the rudder ropes. And they hoisted the foresail to the roo-ahk and made for the beach.

items.name: narrator
items.text: But coming upon a place where two seas met, they grounded the ship and the prow stuck fast and remained immovable, but the stern was broken by the pounding of the surf.
items.kk: But coming upon a place where two seas met, they grounded the ship and the prow stuck fast and remained immovable, but the stern was broken by the pounding of the surf.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And the soldiers intended to kill the prisoners, lest any of them should swim away and escape.
items.kk: And the soldiers intended to kill the prisoners, lest any of them should swim away and escape.

items.name: narrator
items.text: But the captain, intending to save Sha’ul, kept them from their intention and commanded those able to swim to jump first and get to land,
items.kk: But the captain, intending to save Shaul, kept them from their intention and commanded those able to swim to jump first and get to land,

items.name: narrator
items.text: and the rest, some indeed on boards and some on items of the ship. And so it came to be that all reached the land in safety.
items.kk: and the rest, some indeed on boards and some on items of the ship. And so it came to be that all reached the land in safety.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And having come to safety, they then learned that the island was called Melite.
items.kk: And having come to safety, they then learned that the island was called Melite.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And the foreigners showed us extraordinary kindness, for they kindled a fire and received us all, because of the rain that was falling and because of the cold.
items.kk: And the foreigners showed us extraordinary kindness, for they kindled a fire and received us all, because of the rain that was falling and because of the cold.

items.name: narrator
items.text: But Sha’ul, having gathered a bundle of sticks and having laid them on the fire, an adder came out because of the heat and fastened itself on his hand.
items.kk: But Shaul, having gathered a bundle of sticks and having laid them on the fire, an adder came out because of the heat and fastened itself on his hand.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And when the foreigners saw the creature hanging from his hand, they said to each other,
items.kk: And when the foreigners saw the creature hanging from his hand, they said to each other,

items.name: islanders
items.text: “This man is certainly a murderer, whom, though saved from the sea, still right-ruling does not allow to live.”
items.kk: This man is certainly a murderer, whom, though saved from the sea, still right-ruling does not allow to live.

items.name: narrator
items.text: Then, indeed, he shook off the creature into the fire and suffered no evil.
items.kk: Then, indeed, he shook off the creature into the fire and suffered no evil.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And expecting that he would swell up or suddenly fall down dead, they waited for a long time and saw no harm come to him, changing their minds they said that he was a mighty one.
items.kk: And expecting that he would swell up or suddenly fall down dead, they waited for a long time and saw no harm come to him, changing their minds they said that he was a mighty one.

items.name: narrator
items.text: Two hundred and seventy-six. You count them twice, as you counted the fish in Galil. Not one is missing.
items.kk: Two hundred and seventy-six. You count them twice, as you counted the fish in gah-leel. Not one is missing.

items.name: narrator
items.text: The stern is gone. The bow is still fast on the bank where the two seas meet, and the waves are taking her apart plank by plank.
items.kk: The stern is gone. The bow is still fast on the bank where the two seas meet, and the waves are taking her apart plank by plank.

items.name: narrator
items.text: Rome. On the Palatine, where the prologue saw a palisade of huts above the Tiber in the year the Romans count from, the houses of the Caesars stand now. Into this city, eight hundred years on, a prisoner from Yahrushalayim is walking.
items.kk: Rome. On the Palatine, where the prologue saw a palisade of huts above the Tiber in the year the Romans count from, the houses of the Caesars stand now. Into this city, eight hundred years on, a prisoner from yah-roo-shah-lah-yeem is walking.

items.name: narrator
items.text: where we found brothers and were invited to stay with them seven days. And so we went toward Rome.
items.kk: where we found brothers and were invited to stay with them seven days. And so we went toward Rome.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And when the brothers there heard about us, they came to meet us as far as Forum of Appius and Three Taverns. When Sha’ul saw them, he thanked Aluahim and took courage.
items.kk: And when the brothers there heard about us, they came to meet us as far as Forum of Appius and Three Taverns. When Shaul saw them, he thanked al-oo-ah-heem and took courage.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And when we came to Rome, the captain delivered the prisoners to the captain of the guard, but Sha’ul was allowed to stay by himself with the soldier guarding him.
items.kk: And when we came to Rome, the captain delivered the prisoners to the captain of the guard, but Shaul was allowed to stay by himself with the soldier guarding him.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And having appointed him a day, many came to him where he was staying, to whom he was explaining, earnestly witnessing about the reign of Aluahim and persuading them concerning Yahusha from both the Torah of Mosheh and the Naḇi'im, from morning until evening.
items.kk: And having appointed him a day, many came to him where he was staying, to whom he was explaining, earnestly witnessing about the reign of al-oo-ah-heem and persuading them concerning yah-hoo-shah from both the toh-rah of Mosheh and the Nabiim, from morning until evening.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And some indeed were persuaded by what was said, but some believed not.
items.kk: And some indeed were persuaded by what was said, but some believed not.

items.name: narrator
items.text: And Sha’ul stayed two entire years in his own rented house and was receiving all who came to him,
items.kk: And Shaul stayed two entire years in his own rented house and was receiving all who came to him,

items.name: narrator
items.text: proclaiming the reign of Alohimand teaching about the Master Yahusha Mashiach with all boldness, unhindered.
items.kk: proclaiming the reign of Alohimand teaching about the Master yah-hoo-shah mah-shee-ahk with all boldness, unhindered.

items.name: narrator
items.text: Seven hundred years ago a man of your family copied out the words of Yahshayahu in Yahrushalayim. You have seen every one of them come true, and now they are being read aloud in Rome.
items.kk: Seven hundred years ago a man of your family copied out the words of yah-shah-yah-hoo in yah-roo-shah-lah-yeem. You have seen every one of them come true, and now they are being read aloud in Rome.

items.name: narrator
items.text: "With all boldness, unhindered." The streets are full. There is a great deal of city.
items.kk: With all boldness, unhindered. The streets are full. There is a great deal of city.

items.name: narrator
items.text: The end of Act VIII. From Bĕyth Leḥem to Rome — the promise, kept
items.kk: The end of Act eight. From bayt leh-khem to Rome, the promise, kept
